found_values.source: F15 (Research.md:676): '16 cells, 67.2 V at 4.2 V a cell'. A balance lead carries one cell between each pair of adjacent pins. A shift by one pin keeps 4.2 V between neighbours and puts up to 4.2 V on the lowest pin. A reversal swaps the pack end for end. Commit 145e028

found_values.value: the barrier's pack-side current, drawn from the ADBMS1818's 5 V VREG. For the rank-1 ISO7741DWR at VCC2 = 5 V, all channels switching (square wave, CL = 15 pF): ICC2 2.8 mA typical and 4.6 mA maximum at 1 Mbps, and 4.2 mA typical and 6.4 mA maximum at 10 Mbps. DC: 3.7 mA maximum with the inputs high and 5.2 mA maximum with them low. The 1 MHz SPI clock is 2 Mbps, between the two tabulated rates, so 6.4 mA is the bound. The table gives VCC1 = VCC2 = 5 V; mixed 3.3 V and 5 V supplies are not tabulated. Rank 2, ISO6741DWR: 3.0 / 4.5 mA at 1 Mbps and 4.8 / 6.5 mA at 10 Mbps. Rank 3, ISO7041DBQR: 0.167 / 0.211 mA at 1 Mbps with no load. ISO7041 figures at 2 Mbps are not tabulated. The voltage, 5 V from VREG, is the owner's answer

requirements.datasheet: measures up to 18 cells (p. 1). Unused C inputs are shorted to the highest connected cell or left open (p. 86). TME (total measurement error) holds with V+ from 16 to 90 V, C13 at least 2.5 V and C7 at least 1 V (Table 3). With V193's tie, a 1-cell pack at 2.8 V puts C7 and C13 at 2.8 V. Packs under 16 V (1 to 3 cells at 4.2 V, 1 to 5 cells at 2.8 V) need V+ of at least 16 V from another supply; see the report 'monitor supply for small packs'

requirements.name: stack voltage
requirements.datasheet: V+ 16 to 90 V and V+ to C12 at most 40 V for TME (Table 3). At 16 cells × 4.2 V: 67.2 - 50.4 = 16.8 V

requirements.name: input rating
requirements.datasheet: absolute maximum: V+ to V- 112.5 V; C(n) and S(n) -0.3 V to MIN(8 × n, 112.5 V), so C16 is rated 112.5 V; C18 to MIN(V+ + 5.5 V, 112.5 V) (Table 11)

requirements.required: own input apart from the 2S lead
requirements.datasheet: a board arrangement: one IC on the ESC pack's lead only

requirements.name: one connector
requirements.datasheet: C0 to C18 in one IC (p. 1, pin table)

requirements.name: no count setting
requirements.required: no setting; the board ties unused inputs
requirements.datasheet: unused inputs shorted to the highest connected cell are allowed (p. 86). No register sets the count. The tie network is a board circuit the data sheet does not specify

requirements.name: pack-side interface
requirements.required: on the pack negative; direct 4-wire SPI to a digital isolator
requirements.datasheet: ISOMD (pin 55) tied to V- gives 4-wire SPI on CSB, SCK, SDI and SDO (pins 61, 62, 53 and 54), referenced to V-. V- is pins 59 and 60 and the exposed pad (pin table)
requirements.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B pin table p. 12, read 2026-10-02T00:19:24Z

requirements.name: SPI timing
requirements.datasheet: tCLK at least 1 µs; t3 and t4 at least 200 ns; SDI setup and hold (t1, t2) 25 ns each (Table 9); SCK falling edge to SDO valid (t8) 60 ns maximum (Table 10)

requirements.name: isolator supply
requirements.required: VREG also supplies the barrier's pack side
requirements.datasheet: VREG is a 5 V input, 4.5 to 5.5 V (Table 3), made by an NPN driven from DRIVE: DRIVE gives 5.7 V and sources 1 mA, the NPN needs a beta over 40, and 'the peak VREG current requirement of the ADBMS1818 approaches 35 mA'. 'If the VREG pin is required to support any additional load, a transistor with an even higher Beta may be required' (p. 71). The device's own VREG draw in 4-wire SPI is at most 16.5 mA (core, measure) plus 8.1 mA (ISOMD = 0, active, RB1 + RB2 = 2 kΩ) (Table 3). DRIVE is 0 V in the sleep state (p. 25), so an isolator on that VREG is unpowered in sleep; see the report

requirements.name: tap current
requirements.datasheet: C(n) input leakage when not measured is 10 nA typical and ±250 nA maximum over the full range. Input current while measured is ±1 µA typical, with no maximum given. Open-wire detection draws 70 / 100 / 130 µA (Table 1, V+ = 59.4 V). With ADOW at a duty under 76 %, the average stays under 100 µA. The case of V+ below 16 V is not specified

requirements.name: cell resolution
requirements.datasheet: 0.1 mV/bit (Table 1)

requirements.name: error under load
requirements.datasheet: normal-mode TME at 4.2 V: ±3.8 mV at 25 °C and ±4.8 mV over the full range (Table 1). That leaves 1.2 mV for the timing term, which V186 does not fix

requirements.name: cell voltage range
requirements.datasheet: input range C(n-1) to C(n-1) + 5 V. Over the full range: ±2.8 mV at 2.0 V, ±4.0 mV at 3.3 V and ±4.8 mV at 4.2 V (Table 1). No point is given at 2.8 V itself

requirements.name: reading period
requirements.datasheet: 18 cells in normal mode: 2027 / 2343 / 2488 µs from REFUP, plus tREFUP 2.7 / 3.5 / 4.4 ms from standby (Table 4). At most 6.9 ms

requirements.name: sample skew
requirements.datasheet: tSKEW2, cell 18 to cell 1 with ADCV, normal mode: 580 / 670 / 711 µs (Table 4). Not checked

requirements.name: current pairing
requirements.datasheet: no current input; the pairing with the INA228's sample is a firmware and timing matter, not checked

requirements.name: resistance resolution
requirements.datasheet: 0.1 mV/bit over 10 A is 0.01 mΩ

requirements.name: mis-plugged lead
requirements.required: shifted lead and 67.2 V reversed lead
requirements.datasheet: C(n) to C(n-1) -0.3 to 8 V; groups of three -0.3 to 21 V; C0 -0.3 to 6 V (Table 11). A shifted lead stays inside these ratings. Every C and S pin is rated -0.3 V minimum, so a reversed lead passes only with the balance-lead protection left to stage 2 of round 2

report.value: V289 puts the isolator's pack side on the ADBMS1818's VREG. VREG is made from DRIVE through an NPN, and DRIVE is 0 V in the sleep state (p. 25), so the isolator's pack side is unpowered then. The monitor enters sleep tSLEEP = 1.8 to 2.2 s after the last valid command (Table 4). In 4-wire SPI it wakes only on activity on CSB or SCK: a differential SCK - CSB of at least 200 mV for at least 240 ns (Table 7, p. 56). An isolator output with no supply cannot drive that, so the coprocessor cannot wake a sleeping monitor through any candidate. The data sheet allows 'VREG can be powered by an external supply' (p. 25). That would keep the isolator powered, but its quiescent current would then flow from the pack: 2.0 to 5.2 mA for ISO7741, 11 to 19.5 µA for ISO7041 (DC). Keeping the monitor awake with a command every 1.8 s or less needs it awake first. The data sheet text read does not state its state after V+ is applied. The owner decides how VREG is supplied
report.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B pp. 25, 56, Tables 4 and 7, read 2026-10-02T00:19:24Z; ISO7741 SLLSEP4K 5.10; ISO7041 SLLSF54D 7.10

report.value: ISO7741DWR ICC2 at 5 V: 2.8 / 4.6 mA at 1 Mbps, 4.2 / 6.4 mA at 10 Mbps, DC at most 5.2 mA. ISO6741DWR: 3.0 / 4.5 mA, 4.8 / 6.5 mA, DC at most 5.1 mA. ISO7041DBQR: 0.166 / 0.211 mA at 1 Mbps with no load, DC at most 19.5 µA. ADUM1401BRWZ-RL (not shortlisted): 1.2 / 1.8 mA at DC to 2 Mbps (3 V/5 V). The 1 MHz SPI clock is 2 Mbps; the TI tables give 1 and 10 Mbps only

ADBMS1818 VREG at most 16.5 mA (core, measure, full range) + 8.1 mA (ISOMD = 0, active, RB1 + RB2 = 2 kΩ; 3.3 mA with 20 kΩ) + isolator 6.4 mA (ISO7741) = 31.0 mA. The data sheet sizes the DRIVE-and-NPN regulator for a peak 'approaching 35 mA' with an NPN beta over 40, and asks for a higher beta for extra load (p. 71). The NPN is not selected by any function

The ADBMS1818 meets its TME with V+ at 16 to 90 V (Table 3). VREG's NPN collector needs 'a minimum 6 V above V-' (p. 71). Packs of 1 to 3 cells at 4.2 V (12.6 V at most) or 1 to 5 cells at 2.8 V (14.0 V at most) give less. These packs need V+ and the NPN collector fed from a supply referenced to the pack negative, which crosses the 85 V barrier from the board side. No function names that supply or its isolation. A gap for P5 and P6
